newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines cut fares to stimulate traffic.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines cut fares to stimulate traffic.

text.p: By cutting their winter air fares, the leading U.S. airlines are hoping to keep passenger traffic strong to allow them capitalize on the expiration of a federal passenger tax on air travel -- a strategy that proved highly successful last year.

While airlines traditionally offer fare incentives to bolster traffic during the slow winter months, the cuts this year, as well as last, carry special importance as the airlines try to make the most of the expired tax.

As the 10 percent passenger excise tax expires again Tuesday, December 31, airlines will reap the same bonus as last year. Carriers will enjoy a windfall that would normally go to the government to support the Federal Aviation Administration.
The extra revenue and a competitive fare structure could help U.S. carriers match the record financial performance seen in 1996, analysts said.
For each month the tax is lapsed in 1997, airlines' earnings will be about 25 percent to 26 percent higher than if the tax were in effect, said Brian Harris, an airline analyst with Lehman Brothers.
Analysts expect it will take Congress six months to reinstate the tax, compared with an eight-month lapse in 1996.
This season's fare cuts -- up to 40 percent on flights throughout North America and to Europe, Asia and the Caribbean -- match similar offers last year.
While fare cuts are "typical for this time of year," the discounts should keep air traffic strong, said Susan Donofrio, an airline analyst with NatWest Securities.

Delta Air Lines Inc initiated the winter fare sale, which was matched in competitive markets by AMR Corp's American Airlines, UAL Corp's United Airlines, Northwest Airlines Corp and Trans World Airlines Inc.
Delta said sale fares for most markets in the United States and Canada range from $158 to $358 round-trip. Most of the sale fares are good from January 6 through March 15.
The winter sale fares for travel to Mexico, Europe, Russia and Asia, except Japan, offer discounts off the normal excursion fares for travel from January 13 through March 19, Delta said.
